In September, 1975, Westmoreland Resources filed a mining and reclamation plan with the U.S. Geological Survey to mine coal over a 20 year period on a 2,151 acre tract immediately adjacent to the present operation in Tract III. The 2,151 acre tract includes Section 36, on which the coal is owned by the State of Montana and is not subject to Tribal or Federal Jurisdiction. Coal mined from the 2,151 acres would be shipped by rail using the existing railroad facilities. This operation would extract over a 20 year period a maximum of 10 million tons annually by 1981. This proposed mining operation is the subject of an environmental statement currently being prepared under the leadership of the U.S. Geological Survey. Two alternative mining plans included in this proposal outline possible mining areas for a third dragline to attain an eventual production level of 15 million tons by 1989 as stipulated in the Tract III amended lease.
The mining methods most likely to be used in the leased area are best exemplified by Westmoreland's current operations. This method entails removal of the materials overlying the coalbeds along narrow parallel strips which can extend for the length of the property (Figure I-1). The initial strip is generally begun at the limit of the merchantable coal—the limit beyond which the coal is burned or oxidized and of no use as a fuel—and successive cuts are made toward thicker overburden. Successive cuts are made until the outer limit of the merchantable coal, the property line, or the limit of economically recoverable coal is reached.
